checklist.action: gh pr view <n> --repo <owner/repo> --json title,author,state,isDraft,baseRefName,headRefName,headRefOid,mergedAt,mergeable,body,files,reviews,comments,statusCheckRollup — record head_sha_reviewed, base_branch and the PR state in the state file
read the PR description in full; note what it says was run, what was not run, and what it calls unverified

read the existing reviews, review threads and comments (gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>/comments and .../issues/<n>/comments): points already raised and replies to earlier reviews, so the review neither repeats nor ignores them

re-review round: read the author's answers to the previous review (previous_review_url), the threads and the commits since previous_head; note which earlier findings they say they fixed and which they dispute
list the companion PRs, issues and decision records the description names, each with its current state
if the PR is merged, closed or a draft, tell the user now and ask whether to continue: a review of a merged PR is follow-up work, not a merge gate
clone or fetch the repo into <workspace>/repo, never into a checkout or worktree the user works in
git fetch origin +pull/<n>/head:pr-<n> and git fetch origin <base> (the + lets a later round fetch a head the author force-pushed)
behind check: git rev-list --count pr-<n>..origin/<base>; if non-zero, say the branch is behind and review against its merge-base
git diff origin/<base>...pr-<n> --stat, and the full THREE-DOT diff saved to <workspace>/notes/diff.patch; never two-dot

re-review round: save the new commits' diff, git diff <previous_head> pr-<n>, to <workspace>/notes/round-<round>.patch; if previous_head is not an ancestor of pr-<n> (git merge-base --is-ancestor: a rebase or force-push), compare with git range-diff origin/<base>..<previous_head> origin/<base>..pr-<n> instead
predict conflicts: git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only --no-messages pr-<n> origin/<base> (exit 0 clean, 1 conflicts)
read the whole diff, and open every changed source file at the PR head for context, not only the hunks
classify the change: code, config or infrastructure, schema or migration, docs, tests, generated or recorded fixtures; note which part is mechanical
write two to four plain sentences: what the PR does and why

list every claim the change relies on, from the description, code comments, docs and commit messages (versions, the behaviour of other systems, 'X already sets Y', 'nothing else reads Z', test results), into state.claims

re-review round: check each finding carried from the last round (recheck PENDING) against the new commits and the file at the new head; record recheck RESOLVED, OPEN or WITHDRAWN (the author showed it wrong, and the source agrees) with recheck_evidence, through update. done refuses this stage while one is still PENDING

check each claim at its source: the file and line at the PR head, the upstream code at the exact pinned version, the other repo's default branch, or a read-only API call; record the evidence (path:line, URL or command) in state.claims
before citing a file as evidence, confirm it describes the same thing as the claim: the same app, environment, instance and version
mark each claim VERIFIED, REFUTED or UNVERIFIED; a refuted claim that the change depends on is a finding
for a claim that cannot be checked (no access, a blocked command), record why; never fill the gap from memory

re-fetch the base before this stage (git fetch origin <base>); if it moved since stage 2, redo the behind check and merge-tree, and re-read every base line the PR, its claims or the findings cite: a neighbour PR can merge after the author's last push and move those lines

consumers: find everything that reads what changed (other processes that load the same settings, jobs, services, other repos, generated clients) and whether each still works after the change, in the order it deploys
decisions: compare the change with the accepted decision records and docs on the base branch, and the PR with itself (code against its own docs, tests and description); a contradiction is a finding
neighbours: find the other open PRs that touch the same files, and test-merge each with this one
security: authentication, authorization, secrets, data exposure, injection, sensitive values in logs (pipeline-shared, Code Review)
tests: the tests exercise the changed code; note what the description says was not run
CI on the reviewed head: which checks passed, failed, were skipped or are pending

branch rules: gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/rules/branches/<base> (and the branch protection, if readable): required approvals, code-owner review, last-push approval, required review thread resolution, merge queue
if review threads must be resolved before merging, put non-blocking comments in the review body, not in inline threads
code owners: whether the user's approval counts (CODEOWNERS and their team membership), so they know whether it unblocks the merge

re-review round: open the draft with the earlier findings and what became of each (resolved, still open, withdrawn) at the new head, then the new findings; an earlier Must still OPEN keeps the verdict at REQUEST_CHANGES

pick the verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES only for a must-fix (wrong behaviour, security, a deploy break, a contradiction with an accepted decision); APPROVE when only suggestions and nits remain; COMMENT when the review cannot conclude
rank the findings Must, Should and Nit; each says what is wrong, its evidence, its impact and a concrete fix

list what was checked and held, and what was not verified and why; the list states the merge status: current with the base or behind it, merges cleanly or conflicts, and which open PRs it conflicts with
write the review body to <workspace>/draft.md in the voice of the posted review, and any inline comments with path, line and side
present the draft to the user in plain language, with the verdict, and ask whether to post it and as which kind of review
wait for the user's explicit OK for this review, and record their words in state.user_approval; an OK given for another PR does not count

re-fetch the PR right before posting: head SHA, state, merged; if the head moved, review the new commits (three-dot from head_sha_reviewed) and update the draft first; if it was merged or closed, ask before posting
post with gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<n>/reviews: commit_id = head_sha_reviewed, the agreed event, the body from draft.md, and inline comments only as agreed
verify the review exists with the right state and URL, and that each inline comment is anchored to its line; record posted_review_url
with --no-post, or when the user declines, skip posting and leave draft.md for the user
tell the user the outcome in a few lines: the verdict, the link, whether their review unblocks the merge, and what still blocks it
list the follow-ups the review promised (merge order, updates to make after a merge) and offer them
set completed_at and review_verdict, keep the workspace for --resume and for a later round (review_state.py round), and say where it is
